title: Ukraine's Zelenskyy Wants an 'Energy Truce' — No More Striking Power Plants
summary:
Imagine if your town's electricity and heating could be knocked out any night — and winter is coming. That's what's happening in Ukraine right now.

Ukraine's President, Volodymyr Zelenskyy, was in New York for the United Nations General Assembly. He met with US President Donald Trump for 40 minutes. Afterward, Zelenskyy said something big: Ukraine is ready for an 'energy ceasefire.'

What does that mean? If Russia stops attacking Ukraine's power plants, electricity, heating, and water systems, then Ukraine will stop attacking Russia's oil refineries and fuel sites. 'We are ready for energy ceasefire,' Zelenskyy told reporters.

But there's a problem. Last week, the two countries agreed to stop hitting each other's energy facilities — and then the strikes started again almost right away. Zelenskyy also warned that Russia is planning 'a new massive attack' on Ukraine.

Ukraine has been using long-range drones to hit Russian oil refineries far away — one attack even forced Moscow's oil refinery to stop processing crude oil. Trump worries this is making diesel fuel more expensive around the world.

Zelenskyy also asked for more Patriot air-defense missiles to protect Ukraine this winter. But those missiles are running low worldwide because of the wars in Ukraine and Iran. So the question is: can a truce actually hold this time?
why_it_matters: It shows how a war far away can change prices and supplies for everyone — and how hard it is to make a promise of peace actually stick.

keywords.explanation: An agreement between two fighting countries to stop attacking each other's power stations and fuel places.
Big factories that turn thick crude oil into useful fuels like petrol and diesel.
Oil pumped straight out of the ground that has not yet been turned into fuel.
Small flying machines with no pilot inside that can travel very far to reach a target.
Special rockets that fly up to knock down incoming planes or missiles and protect a city.
A type of fuel used by trucks, buses, ships and some trains.

background_read: Volodymyr Zelenskyy (Ukraine's president, in office since 2019) leads a country in Eastern Europe that Russia invaded in 2022, and the war is still going on.
The United Nations (a group where almost all countries meet to talk about world problems) holds a big meeting in New York every September, which is why the two presidents met there.
Patriot missiles are made in the United States and are one of the best ways to knock down incoming rockets, so many countries want them — but there are only so many to go around.
Article_Structure: WHO: Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, US President Donald Trump, and Russia, which keeps attacking Ukraine's energy system.
WHAT: After a 40-minute meeting with Trump, Zelenskyy offered an 'energy ceasefire' — Ukraine stops hitting Russian oil refineries if Russia stops hitting Ukraine's power, heat and water.
WHERE: At the United Nations General Assembly in New York, while the fighting and drone strikes continue back in Ukraine and Russia.
WHY: Because winter is coming, a last truce quickly broke down, and Zelenskyy needs Patriot missiles to protect Ukraine's cities.

perspectives.description: Zelenskyy says Ukraine is ready to stop attacking energy targets, but only if Russia stops first — and he needs more air-defense missiles before winter.
Trump is worried that drone strikes on refineries push up the price of diesel fuel all over the world, so he wants the hitting to stop.
The last energy deal fell apart almost immediately, so some people think both sides will keep striking no matter what they promise.
